prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1303; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received today for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. No issues with the policy itself were found at intake.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Officers' observations of the scene line up with the parties' descriptions.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos and spoke with two independent witnesses, both of whom describe the accident the same way the claimant and the other driver did. Their accounts are consistent on the sequence of events.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The damage is mostly on the driver's side and is in line with the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 6: Claimant reported a concussion. The injury fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and the medical file reflects a usual course of care that tapered as the patient improved.

Entry 7: Medical history shows a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully with no ongoing complaints. Noted for completeness and reviewed with the treating records.

Entry 8: Claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far, including the initial report, the recorded statement, and the follow-up call with counsel present.

Entry 9: Counsel has requested a copy of the claim file and the repair estimate. Sent both through the approved channel and confirmed receipt.

Entry 10: Nothing so far suggests the damage predates the coverage period. Claim remains open pending final medical review and the repair invoice.
